# f5xc_workload (Data Source)

Workload is used to configure and deploy a workload in Virtual Kubernetes. A workload can be<br>either a service or stateful service or a batch job. Services and jobs can be deployed on<br>regional edges or customer sites. Services can be exposed in-cluster or by L7 or L4<br>load balancer on Internet or on sites using an advertise policy.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Example: Workload - Full

data "f5xc_workload" "example" {
  name      = f5xc_workload.example.name
  namespace = f5xc_workload.example.namespace
}
```

- `service` (Attributes) Service Service does not maintain per replica state, however it can be configured to use persistent storage that is shared amongst all the replicas. - `stateful_service` (Attributes) Stateful Service Stateful Service maintains per replica state and each replica has its own persistent storage. ### Nested Schema for `workload_choice.job.containers.liveness_check`

Read-Only:

- `health_check_choice` (Attributes) HealthCheckChoice Specifies action taken to determine health of a container (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--job--containers--liveness_check--health_check_choice))
- `healthy_threshold` (Number) HealthyThreshold Number of consecutive successful responses after having failed before declaring healthy. In other words, this is the number of healthy health checks required before marking healthy. Note that during startup and liveliness, only a single successful health check is required to mark a container healthy.
- `initial_delay` (Number) InitialDelay Number of seconds after the container has started before health checks are initiated
- `interval` (Number) Interval Time interval in seconds between two health check requests.
- `timeout` (Number) Timeout Timeout in seconds to wait for successful response. In other words, it is the time to wait for a health check response. If the timeout is reached the health check attempt will be considered a failure.
- `unhealthy_threshold` (Number) UnhealthyThreshold Number of consecutive failed responses before declaring unhealthy. In other words, this is the number of unhealthy health checks required before a container is marked unhealthy.

### Nested Schema for `workload_choice.service.advertise_options.advertise_choice.advertise_custom.ports.advertise_choice.http_loadbalancer`

Read-Only:

- `domains` (List of String) Domains A list of domains (host/authority header) that will be matched to loadbalancer. Wildcard hosts are supported in the suffix or prefix form Domain search order: 1. Exact domain names: ``www.foo.com``. 2. Prefix domain wildcards: ``*.foo.com`` or ``*.bar.foo.com``. 3. Special wildcard ``*`` matching any domain. Wildcard will not match empty string. e.g. ``*.foo.com`` will match ``bar.foo.com`` and ``baz-bar.foo.com`` but not ``.foo.com``. The longest wildcards match first. Wildcards must match a whole DNS label. e.g. ``*.foo.com`` and *.bar.foo.com are valid, however ``*bar.foo.com`` or ``*-bar.foo.com`` is invalid Domains are also used for SNI matching if the loadbalancer type is HTTPS Domains also indicate the list of names for which DNS resolution will be done by VER
- `loadbalancer_type_choice` (Attributes) Proxy choice Type of Load Balancer can be 'http' or 'https' (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice))
- `route_choice` (Attributes) Route Choice Routes for this load balancer (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--route_choice))

- `https` (Attributes) HTTPS HTTPS Load balancer with a custom public/private certificate. This is also known as BYOC (Bring Your Own Certificate). User is responsible for managing DNS to this Load Balancer. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https))
- `https_auto_cert` (Attributes) HTTPS HTTPS Load balancer with automatic public certificate provisioning. This requires the domain to be delegated to F5XC using Delegated Domain feature. DNS records will be managed by Volterra. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert))

As a prerequisite, the domain must be delegated to F5 Distributed Cloud using Delegated domain feature or a DNS CNAME record should be created in your DNS provider's portal.

Read-Only:

- `coalescing_options` (Attributes) TLS Coalescing options Options for coalescing TLS for multiple HTTPS Load Balancers (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--coalescing_options))
- `connection_idle_timeout` (Number) Connection Idle Timeout The idle timeout for downstream connections. The idle timeout is defined as the period in which there are no active requests. When the idle timeout is reached the connection will be closed. Note that request based timeouts mean that HTTP/2 PINGs will not keep the connection alive. This is specified in milliseconds. The default value is 2 minutes.
- `default_lb_choice` (Attributes) Default Load Balancer Designate the Load balancer as default for clients that don't present the SNI header in TLS handshake. Read-Only:

- `header_transformation` (Attributes) Header transformation Two mutually exclusive types of header key formatters are supported: Stateless (Default and Proper Case) and Stateful (Preserve Case) formatters. When a Stateless formatter is selected, it applies to response headers sent to the client and when a Stateful formatter is selected, it applies to the upstream request headers. It's essential to ensure that the same formatter type (either stateless or stateful) is applied on origin pool. If different formatter types are applied, only the stateful formatter will take effect, and the stateless formatter will be disregarded. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--http_protocol_options--http_protocol_choice--http_protocol_enable_v1_only--header_transformation))

Read-Only:

- `header_transformation_choice` (Attributes) Header transformation Select header transformation options for HTTP/1.1 (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--http_protocol_options--http_protocol_choice--http_protocol_enable_v1_only--header_transformation--header_transformation_choice))

Read-Only:

- `default_header_transformation` (Boolean) Default header transformation Normalize the headers to lower case
- `legacy_header_transformation` (Boolean) Legacy header transformations Use old header transformation if configured earlier
- `preserve_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Preserve case header transformation Preserves the original case of headers without any modifications.
- `proper_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Proper case header transformation Normalize the headers to proper case words. The first character and any character following a special character will be capitalized if it’s an alpha character. For example, “content-type” becomes “Content-Type”, and “foo$b#$are” becomes “Foo$B#$Are”

Read-Only:

- `append_server_name` (String) append_server_name Define the header value for the header name 'server'. If header value is already present, it is not overwritten and passed as-is.
- `default_header` (Boolean) default_header Response header name is 'server' and value is 'volt-adc'
- `pass_through` (Boolean) pass_through Pass existing server header as is. If server header is absent, a new header is not appended.
- `server_name` (String) server_name Define the header value for the header name 'server'. This will overwrite existing values, if any, for the server header.

### Nested Schema for `workload_choice.service.advertise_options.advertise_choice.advertise_custom.ports.advertise_choice.http_loadbalancer.loadbalancer_type_choice.https.tls_certificates_choice.tls_parameters.tls_certificates.ocsp_stapling_choice`

Read-Only:

- `custom_hash_algorithms` (Attributes) Use Custom Order for Hash Algorithms Use hash algorithms in the custom order. F5XC will try to fetch ocsp response from the CA in the given order. Additionally, LoadBalancer will not become active until ocspResponse cannot be fetched if the certificate has MustStaple extension set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--tls_certificates_choice--tls_parameters--tls_certificates--ocsp_stapling_choice--custom_hash_algorithms))
- `disable_ocsp_stapling` (Boolean) Disable OCSP Stapling Disable OCSP Stapling. F5XC will not fetch and staple OCSP Response for this certificate. This is the default behavior if no choice is selected.
- `use_system_defaults` (Boolean) Fetch with F5XC default settings Use F5XC Default Settings to fetch and staple OCSP Response. OCSP Response will be stapled if it can be fetched. Additionally, LoadBalancer will not become active until ocspResponse cannot be fetched if the certificate has MustStaple extension set. F5XC will try to fetch OCSPResponse with sha256 and sha1 as HashAlgorithm, in that order.

Read-Only:

- `header_transformation` (Attributes) Header transformation Two mutually exclusive types of header key formatters are supported: Stateless (Default and Proper Case) and Stateful (Preserve Case) formatters. When a Stateless formatter is selected, it applies to response headers sent to the client and when a Stateful formatter is selected, it applies to the upstream request headers. It's essential to ensure that the same formatter type (either stateless or stateful) is applied on origin pool. If different formatter types are applied, only the stateful formatter will take effect, and the stateless formatter will be disregarded. - `legacy_header_transformation` (Boolean) Legacy header transformations Use old header transformation if configured earlier
- `preserve_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Preserve case header transformation Preserves the original case of headers without any modifications.
- `proper_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Proper case header transformation Normalize the headers to proper case words. The first character and any character following a special character will be capitalized if it’s an alpha character. For example, “content-type” becomes “Content-Type”, and “foo$b#$are” becomes “Foo$B#$Are”

Read-Only:

- `domains` (List of String) Domains A list of domains (host/authority header) that will be matched to loadbalancer. Wildcard hosts are supported in the suffix or prefix form Domain search order: 1. Exact domain names: ``www.foo.com``. 2. Prefix domain wildcards: ``*.foo.com`` or ``*.bar.foo.com``. 3. Special wildcard ``*`` matching any domain. Wildcard will not match empty string. e.g. ``*.foo.com`` will match ``bar.foo.com`` and ``baz-bar.foo.com`` but not ``.foo.com``. The longest wildcards match first. Wildcards must match a whole DNS label. e.g. ``*.foo.com`` and *.bar.foo.com are valid, however ``*bar.foo.com`` or ``*-bar.foo.com`` is invalid Domains are also used for SNI matching if the loadbalancer type is HTTPS Domains also indicate the list of names for which DNS resolution will be done by VER
- `loadbalancer_type_choice` (Attributes) Proxy choice Type of Load Balancer can be 'http' or 'https' (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_on_public--advertise_choice--multi_ports--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice))
- `route_choice` (Attributes) Route Choice Routes for this load balancer (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_on_public--advertise_choice--multi_ports--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--route_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_on_public--advertise_choice--multi_ports--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice"></a>

- `http` (Attributes) HTTP HTTP Load balancer. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_on_public--advertise_choice--multi_ports--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--http))
- `https` (Attributes) HTTPS HTTPS Load balancer with a custom public/private certificate. This is also known as BYOC (Bring Your Own Certificate). User is responsible for managing DNS to this Load Balancer. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_on_public--advertise_choice--multi_ports--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https))
- `https_auto_cert` (Attributes) HTTPS HTTPS Load balancer with automatic public certificate provisioning. This requires the domain to be delegated to F5XC using Delegated Domain feature. DNS records will be managed by Volterra. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_on_public--advertise_choice--multi_ports--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert))

As a prerequisite, the domain must be delegated to F5 Distributed Cloud using Delegated domain feature or a DNS CNAME record should be created in your DNS provider's portal.

- `coalescing_options` (Attributes) TLS Coalescing options Options for coalescing TLS for multiple HTTPS Load Balancers (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_on_public--advertise_choice--multi_ports--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--coalescing_options))
- `connection_idle_timeout` (Number) Connection Idle Timeout The idle timeout for downstream connections. The idle timeout is defined as the period in which there are no active requests. When the idle timeout is reached the connection will be closed. Note that request based timeouts mean that HTTP/2 PINGs will not keep the connection alive. This is specified in milliseconds. The default value is 2 minutes.
- `default_lb_choice` (Attributes) Default Load Balancer Designate the Load balancer as default for clients that don't present the SNI header in TLS handshake. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_on_public--advertise_choice--multi_ports--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--default_lb_choice))

- `http_redirect` (Boolean) HTTP Redirect Redirect HTTP traffic to HTTPS
- `path_normalize_choice` (Attributes) Normalize Path URI Path is normalized and adjacent slashes in the path are merged into one. The platform does not perform case normalization. - `header_transformation` (Attributes) Header transformation Two mutually exclusive types of header key formatters are supported: Stateless (Default and Proper Case) and Stateful (Preserve Case) formatters. When a Stateless formatter is selected, it applies to response headers sent to the client and when a Stateful formatter is selected, it applies to the upstream request headers. It's essential to ensure that the same formatter type (either stateless or stateful) is applied on origin pool. If different formatter types are applied, only the stateful formatter will take effect, and the stateless formatter will be disregarded. Read-Only:

- `custom_hash_algorithms` (Attributes) Use Custom Order for Hash Algorithms Use hash algorithms in the custom order. F5XC will try to fetch ocsp response from the CA in the given order. Additionally, LoadBalancer will not become active until ocspResponse cannot be fetched if the certificate has MustStaple extension set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_on_public--advertise_choice--multi_ports--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--tls_certificates_choice--tls_parameters--tls_certificates--ocsp_stapling_choice--custom_hash_algorithms))
- `disable_ocsp_stapling` (Boolean) Disable OCSP Stapling Disable OCSP Stapling. F5XC will not fetch and staple OCSP Response for this certificate. This is the default behavior if no choice is selected.
- `use_system_defaults` (Boolean) Fetch with F5XC default settings Use F5XC Default Settings to fetch and staple OCSP Response. OCSP Response will be stapled if it can be fetched. Additionally, LoadBalancer will not become active until ocspResponse cannot be fetched if the certificate has MustStaple extension set. F5XC will try to fetch OCSPResponse with sha256 and sha1 as HashAlgorithm, in that order.

Read-Only:

- `header_transformation` (Attributes) Header transformation Two mutually exclusive types of header key formatters are supported: Stateless (Default and Proper Case) and Stateful (Preserve Case) formatters. When a Stateless formatter is selected, it applies to response headers sent to the client and when a Stateful formatter is selected, it applies to the upstream request headers. It's essential to ensure that the same formatter type (either stateless or stateful) is applied on origin pool. If different formatter types are applied, only the stateful formatter will take effect, and the stateless formatter will be disregarded. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_on_public--advertise_choice--multi_ports--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert--http_protocol_options--http_protocol_choice--http_protocol_enable_v1_only--header_transformation))

- `legacy_header_transformation` (Boolean) Legacy header transformations Use old header transformation if configured earlier
- `preserve_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Preserve case header transformation Preserves the original case of headers without any modifications.
- `proper_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Proper case header transformation Normalize the headers to proper case words. For example, “content-type” becomes “Content-Type”, and “foo$b#$are” becomes “Foo$B#$Are”

- `domains` (List of String) Domains A list of domains (host/authority header) that will be matched to loadbalancer. Wildcard hosts are supported in the suffix or prefix form Domain search order: 1. Exact domain names: ``www.foo.com``. 2. Prefix domain wildcards: ``*.foo.com`` or ``*.bar.foo.com``. 3. Special wildcard ``*`` matching any domain. Wildcard will not match empty string. e.g. ``*.foo.com`` will match ``bar.foo.com`` and ``baz-bar.foo.com`` but not ``.foo.com``. The longest wildcards match first. Wildcards must match a whole DNS label. e.g. ``*.foo.com`` and *.bar.foo.com are valid, however ``*bar.foo.com`` or ``*-bar.foo.com`` is invalid Domains are also used for SNI matching if the loadbalancer type is HTTPS Domains also indicate the list of names for which DNS resolution will be done by VER

- `header_transformation` (Attributes) Header transformation Two mutually exclusive types of header key formatters are supported: Stateless (Default and Proper Case) and Stateful (Preserve Case) formatters. When a Stateless formatter is selected, it applies to response headers sent to the client and when a Stateful formatter is selected, it applies to the upstream request headers. It's essential to ensure that the same formatter type (either stateless or stateful) is applied on origin pool. If different formatter types are applied, only the stateful formatter will take effect, and the stateless formatter will be disregarded. Read-Only:

- `custom_hash_algorithms` (Attributes) Use Custom Order for Hash Algorithms Use hash algorithms in the custom order. F5XC will try to fetch ocsp response from the CA in the given order. Additionally, LoadBalancer will not become active until ocspResponse cannot be fetched if the certificate has MustStaple extension set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_on_public--advertise_choice--port--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--tls_certificates_choice--tls_parameters--tls_certificates--ocsp_stapling_choice--custom_hash_algorithms))
- `disable_ocsp_stapling` (Boolean) Disable OCSP Stapling Disable OCSP Stapling. F5XC will not fetch and staple OCSP Response for this certificate. This is the default behavior if no choice is selected.
- `use_system_defaults` (Boolean) Fetch with F5XC default settings Use F5XC Default Settings to fetch and staple OCSP Response. OCSP Response will be stapled if it can be fetched. Additionally, LoadBalancer will not become active until ocspResponse cannot be fetched if the certificate has MustStaple extension set. F5XC will try to fetch OCSPResponse with sha256 and sha1 as HashAlgorithm, in that order.

- `header_transformation` (Attributes) Header transformation Two mutually exclusive types of header key formatters are supported: Stateless (Default and Proper Case) and Stateful (Preserve Case) formatters. When a Stateless formatter is selected, it applies to response headers sent to the client and when a Stateful formatter is selected, it applies to the upstream request headers. It's essential to ensure that the same formatter type (either stateless or stateful) is applied on origin pool. If different formatter types are applied, only the stateful formatter will take effect, and the stateless formatter will be disregarded. <a id="nestedatt--workload_choice--service--containers--liveness_check"></a>
### Nested Schema for `workload_choice.service.containers.liveness_check`

Read-Only:

- `health_check_choice` (Attributes) HealthCheckChoice Specifies action taken to determine health of a container (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--containers--liveness_check--health_check_choice))
- `healthy_threshold` (Number) HealthyThreshold Number of consecutive successful responses after having failed before declaring healthy. In other words, this is the number of healthy health checks required before marking healthy. Note that during startup and liveliness, only a single successful health check is required to mark a container healthy.
- `initial_delay` (Number) InitialDelay Number of seconds after the container has started before health checks are initiated
- `interval` (Number) Interval Time interval in seconds between two health check requests.
- `timeout` (Number) Timeout Timeout in seconds to wait for successful response. In other words, it is the time to wait for a health check response. If the timeout is reached the health check attempt will be considered a failure.
- `unhealthy_threshold` (Number) UnhealthyThreshold Number of consecutive failed responses before declaring unhealthy. In other words, this is the number of unhealthy health checks required before a container is marked unhealthy.

<a id="nestedatt--workload_choice--service--containers--liveness_check--health_check_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `workload_choice.service.containers.liveness_check.health_check_choice`

Read-Only:

- `exec_health_check` (Attributes) ExecHealthCheck Specifies the run in container action to use for health check requests Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--containers--liveness_check--health_check_choice--exec_health_check))
- `http_health_check` (Attributes) HttpHealthCheck Specifies details for HTTP GET health check requests (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--containers--liveness_check--health_check_choice--http_health_check))
- `tcp_health_check` (Attributes) TCPHealthCheck Specifies port to use for TCP connection for health checks (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--service--containers--liveness_check--health_check_choice--tcp_health_check))

<a id="nestedatt--workload_choice--service--containers--liveness_check--health_check_choice--exec_health_check"></a>
### Nested Schema for `workload_choice.service.containers.liveness_check.health_check_choice.exec_health_check`

Read-Only:

- `command` (List of String) Command Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command  is root ('/') in the container's filesystem. The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions ('|', etc) won't work. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell.

### Nested Schema for `workload_choice.simple_service.advertise_choice`

Read-Only:

- `do_not_advertise` (Boolean) Do Not Advertise Do not advertise the service
- `simple_advertise` (Attributes) Advertise Simple Service Domains and service port to advertise on Internet via HTTP loadbalancer using port 80 (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--simple_service--advertise_choice--simple_advertise))

<a id="nestedatt--workload_choice--simple_service--advertise_choice--simple_advertise"></a>
### Nested Schema for `workload_choice.simple_service.advertise_choice.simple_advertise`

Read-Only:

- `domains` (List of String) Domains A list of Domains (host/authority header) that will be matched to Load Balancer. Wildcard hosts are supported in the suffix or prefix form Supported Domains and search order: 1. Exact Domain names: www.foo.com. 2. Domains starting with a Wildcard: *.foo.com. Not supported Domains: - Just a Wildcard: * - A Wildcard and TLD with no root Domain: *.com. - A Wildcard not matching a whole DNS label. e.g. *.foo.com and *.bar.foo.com are valid Wildcards however *bar.foo.com, *-bar.foo.com, and bar*.foo.com are all invalid. Additional notes: A Wildcard will not match empty string. e.g. *.foo.com will match bar.foo.com and baz-bar.foo.com but not .foo.com. The longest Wildcards match first. Only a single virtual host in the entire route configuration can match on *. Also a Domain must be unique across all virtual hosts within an advertise policy. Domains are also used for SNI matching if the Load Balancer type is HTTPS. Domains also indicate the list of names for which DNS resolution will be automatically resolved to IP addresses by the system.
- `service_port` (Number) Service Port Service port to advertise on Internet via HTTP loadbalancer using port 80

<a id="nestedatt--workload_choice--simple_service--container--liveness_check"></a>
### Nested Schema for `workload_choice.simple_service.container.liveness_check`

Read-Only:

- `health_check_choice` (Attributes) HealthCheckChoice Specifies action taken to determine health of a container (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--simple_service--container--liveness_check--health_check_choice))
- `healthy_threshold` (Number) HealthyThreshold Number of consecutive successful responses after having failed before declaring healthy. In other words, this is the number of healthy health checks required before marking healthy. Note that during startup and liveliness, only a single successful health check is required to mark a container healthy.
- `initial_delay` (Number) InitialDelay Number of seconds after the container has started before health checks are initiated
- `interval` (Number) Interval Time interval in seconds between two health check requests.
- `timeout` (Number) Timeout Timeout in seconds to wait for successful response. In other words, it is the time to wait for a health check response. If the timeout is reached the health check attempt will be considered a failure.
- `unhealthy_threshold` (Number) UnhealthyThreshold Number of consecutive failed responses before declaring unhealthy. In other words, this is the number of unhealthy health checks required before a container is marked unhealthy.

<a id="nestedatt--workload_choice--simple_service--container--liveness_check--health_check_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `workload_choice.simple_service.container.liveness_check.health_check_choice`

Read-Only:

- `exec_health_check` (Attributes) ExecHealthCheck Specifies the run in container action to use for health check requests Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--simple_service--container--liveness_check--health_check_choice--exec_health_check))
- `http_health_check` (Attributes) HttpHealthCheck Specifies details for HTTP GET health check requests (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--simple_service--container--liveness_check--health_check_choice--http_health_check))
- `tcp_health_check` (Attributes) TCPHealthCheck Specifies port to use for TCP connection for health checks (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--simple_service--container--liveness_check--health_check_choice--tcp_health_check))

<a id="nestedatt--workload_choice--simple_service--container--liveness_check--health_check_choice--exec_health_check"></a>
### Nested Schema for `workload_choice.simple_service.container.liveness_check.health_check_choice.exec_health_check`

Read-Only:

- `command` (List of String) Command Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command  is root ('/') in the container's filesystem. The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions ('|', etc) won't work. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell.


<a id="nestedatt--workload_choice--simple_service--container--liveness_check--health_check_choice--http_health_check"></a>

- `path` (String) Path Path to access on the HTTP server.

### Nested Schema for `workload_choice.stateful_service.advertise_options.advertise_choice.advertise_custom.ports.advertise_choice.http_loadbalancer`

Read-Only:

- `domains` (List of String) Domains A list of domains (host/authority header) that will be matched to loadbalancer. Wildcard hosts are supported in the suffix or prefix form Domain search order: 1. Exact domain names: ``www.foo.com``. 2. Prefix domain wildcards: ``*.foo.com`` or ``*.bar.foo.com``. 3. Special wildcard ``*`` matching any domain. Wildcard will not match empty string. e.g. ``*.foo.com`` will match ``bar.foo.com`` and ``baz-bar.foo.com`` but not ``.foo.com``. The longest wildcards match first. Wildcards must match a whole DNS label. e.g. ``*.foo.com`` and *.bar.foo.com are valid, however ``*bar.foo.com`` or ``*-bar.foo.com`` is invalid Domains are also used for SNI matching if the loadbalancer type is HTTPS Domains also indicate the list of names for which DNS resolution will be done by VER
- `loadbalancer_type_choice` (Attributes) Proxy choice Type of Load Balancer can be 'http' or 'https' (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice))
- `route_choice` (Attributes) Route Choice Routes for this load balancer (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--route_choice))

- `https` (Attributes) HTTPS HTTPS Load balancer with a custom public/private certificate. This is also known as BYOC (Bring Your Own Certificate). User is responsible for managing DNS to this Load Balancer. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https))

DNS records will be managed by Volterra. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert))

Read-Only:

- `coalescing_options` (Attributes) TLS Coalescing options Options for coalescing TLS for multiple HTTPS Load Balancers (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--coalescing_options))
- `connection_idle_timeout` (Number) Connection Idle Timeout The idle timeout for downstream connections. The idle timeout is defined as the period in which there are no active requests. When the idle timeout is reached the connection will be closed. Note that request based timeouts mean that HTTP/2 PINGs will not keep the connection alive. This is specified in milliseconds. The default value is 2 minutes.
- `default_lb_choice` (Attributes) Default Load Balancer Designate the Load balancer as default for clients that don't present the SNI header in TLS handshake. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--default_lb_choice))

- `http_redirect` (Boolean) HTTP Redirect Redirect HTTP traffic to HTTPS
- `path_normalize_choice` (Attributes) Normalize Path URI Path is normalized and adjacent slashes in the path are merged into one. The platform does not perform case normalization. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--path_normalize_choice))

Read-Only:

- `header_transformation` (Attributes) Header transformation Two mutually exclusive types of header key formatters are supported: Stateless (Default and Proper Case) and Stateful (Preserve Case) formatters. When a Stateless formatter is selected, it applies to response headers sent to the client and when a Stateful formatter is selected, it applies to the upstream request headers. It's essential to ensure that the same formatter type (either stateless or stateful) is applied on origin pool. If different formatter types are applied, only the stateful formatter will take effect, and the stateless formatter will be disregarded. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--http_protocol_options--http_protocol_choice--http_protocol_enable_v1_only--header_transformation))

Read-Only:

- `default_header_transformation` (Boolean) Default header transformation Normalize the headers to lower case
- `legacy_header_transformation` (Boolean) Legacy header transformations Use old header transformation if configured earlier
- `preserve_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Preserve case header transformation Preserves the original case of headers without any modifications.
- `proper_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Proper case header transformation Normalize the headers to proper case words. The first character and any character following a special character will be capitalized if it’s an alpha character. For example, “content-type” becomes “Content-Type”, and “foo$b#$are” becomes “Foo$B#$Are”

### Nested Schema for `workload_choice.stateful_service.advertise_options.advertise_choice.advertise_custom.ports.advertise_choice.http_loadbalancer.loadbalancer_type_choice.https.tls_certificates_choice.tls_parameters.tls_certificates.ocsp_stapling_choice`

Read-Only:

- `custom_hash_algorithms` (Attributes) Use Custom Order for Hash Algorithms Use hash algorithms in the custom order. F5XC will try to fetch ocsp response from the CA in the given order. Additionally, LoadBalancer will not become active until ocspResponse cannot be fetched if the certificate has MustStaple extension set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_custom--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--tls_certificates_choice--tls_parameters--tls_certificates--ocsp_stapling_choice--custom_hash_algorithms))
- `disable_ocsp_stapling` (Boolean) Disable OCSP Stapling Disable OCSP Stapling. F5XC will not fetch and staple OCSP Response for this certificate. This is the default behavior if no choice is selected.
- `use_system_defaults` (Boolean) Fetch with F5XC default settings Use F5XC Default Settings to fetch and staple OCSP Response. OCSP Response will be stapled if it can be fetched. Additionally, LoadBalancer will not become active until ocspResponse cannot be fetched if the certificate has MustStaple extension set. F5XC will try to fetch OCSPResponse with sha256 and sha1 as HashAlgorithm, in that order.

- `header_transformation` (Attributes) Header transformation Two mutually exclusive types of header key formatters are supported: Stateless (Default and Proper Case) and Stateful (Preserve Case) formatters. When a Stateless formatter is selected, it applies to response headers sent to the client and when a Stateful formatter is selected, it applies to the upstream request headers. It's essential to ensure that the same formatter type (either stateless or stateful) is applied on origin pool. If different formatter types are applied, only the stateful formatter will take effect, and the stateless formatter will be disregarded. - `legacy_header_transformation` (Boolean) Legacy header transformations Use old header transformation if configured earlier
- `preserve_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Preserve case header transformation Preserves the original case of headers without any modifications.
- `proper_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Proper case header transformation Normalize the headers to proper case words. The first character and any character following a special character will be capitalized if it’s an alpha character. For example, “content-type” becomes “Content-Type”, and “foo$b#$are” becomes “Foo$B#$Are”

Read-Only:

- `domains` (List of String) Domains A list of domains (host/authority header) that will be matched to loadbalancer. Wildcard hosts are supported in the suffix or prefix form Domain search order: 1. Exact domain names: ``www.foo.com``. 2. Prefix domain wildcards: ``*.foo.com`` or ``*.bar.foo.com``. 3. Special wildcard ``*`` matching any domain. Wildcard will not match empty string. e.g. ``*.foo.com`` will match ``bar.foo.com`` and ``baz-bar.foo.com`` but not ``.foo.com``. The longest wildcards match first. Wildcards must match a whole DNS label. e.g. ``*.foo.com`` and *.bar.foo.com are valid, however ``*bar.foo.com`` or ``*-bar.foo.com`` is invalid Domains are also used for SNI matching if the loadbalancer type is HTTPS Domains also indicate the list of names for which DNS resolution will be done by VER
- `loadbalancer_type_choice` (Attributes) Proxy choice Type of Load Balancer can be 'http' or 'https' (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_on_public--advertise_choice--multi_ports--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice))
- `route_choice` (Attributes) Route Choice Routes for this load balancer (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_on_public--advertise_choice--multi_ports--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--route_choice))

- `https` (Attributes) HTTPS HTTPS Load balancer with a custom public/private certificate. This is also known as BYOC (Bring Your Own Certificate). Read-Only:

- `header_transformation` (Attributes) Header transformation Two mutually exclusive types of header key formatters are supported: Stateless (Default and Proper Case) and Stateful (Preserve Case) formatters. When a Stateless formatter is selected, it applies to response headers sent to the client and when a Stateful formatter is selected, it applies to the upstream request headers. It's essential to ensure that the same formatter type (either stateless or stateful) is applied on origin pool. If different formatter types are applied, only the stateful formatter will take effect, and the stateless formatter will be disregarded. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_on_public--advertise_choice--multi_ports--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--http_protocol_options--http_protocol_choice--http_protocol_enable_v1_only--header_transformation))

- `default_header_transformation` (Boolean) Default header transformation Normalize the headers to lower case
- `legacy_header_transformation` (Boolean) Legacy header transformations Use old header transformation if configured earlier
- `preserve_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Preserve case header transformation Preserves the original case of headers without any modifications.
- `proper_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Proper case header transformation Normalize the headers to proper case words. The first character and any character following a special character will be capitalized if it’s an alpha character. For example, “content-type” becomes “Content-Type”, and “foo$b#$are” becomes “Foo$B#$Are”

- `custom_hash_algorithms` (Attributes) Use Custom Order for Hash Algorithms Use hash algorithms in the custom order. F5XC will try to fetch ocsp response from the CA in the given order. Additionally, LoadBalancer will not become active until ocspResponse cannot be fetched if the certificate has MustStaple extension set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_on_public--advertise_choice--multi_ports--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--tls_certificates_choice--tls_parameters--tls_certificates--ocsp_stapling_choice--custom_hash_algorithms))
- `disable_ocsp_stapling` (Boolean) Disable OCSP Stapling Disable OCSP Stapling. F5XC will not fetch and staple OCSP Response for this certificate. This is the default behavior if no choice is selected.
- `use_system_defaults` (Boolean) Fetch with F5XC default settings Use F5XC Default Settings to fetch and staple OCSP Response. OCSP Response will be stapled if it can be fetched. Additionally, LoadBalancer will not become active until ocspResponse cannot be fetched if the certificate has MustStaple extension set. F5XC will try to fetch OCSPResponse with sha256 and sha1 as HashAlgorithm, in that order.

Read-Only:

- `header_transformation` (Attributes) Header transformation Two mutually exclusive types of header key formatters are supported: Stateless (Default and Proper Case) and Stateful (Preserve Case) formatters. When a Stateless formatter is selected, it applies to response headers sent to the client and when a Stateful formatter is selected, it applies to the upstream request headers. It's essential to ensure that the same formatter type (either stateless or stateful) is applied on origin pool. If different formatter types are applied, only the stateful formatter will take effect, and the stateless formatter will be disregarded. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--advertise_options--advertise_choice--advertise_on_public--advertise_choice--multi_ports--ports--advertise_choice--http_loadbalancer--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert--http_protocol_options--http_protocol_choice--http_protocol_enable_v1_only--header_transformation))

- `legacy_header_transformation` (Boolean) Legacy header transformations Use old header transformation if configured earlier
- `preserve_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Preserve case header transformation Preserves the original case of headers without any modifications.
- `proper_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Proper case header transformation Normalize the headers to proper case words. - `domains` (List of String) Domains A list of domains (host/authority header) that will be matched to loadbalancer. Wildcard hosts are supported in the suffix or prefix form Domain search order: 1. Exact domain names: ``www.foo.com``. 2. Prefix domain wildcards: ``*.foo.com`` or ``*.bar.foo.com``. 3. Special wildcard ``*`` matching any domain. Wildcard will not match empty string. e.g. ``*.foo.com`` will match ``bar.foo.com`` and ``baz-bar.foo.com`` but not ``.foo.com``. The longest wildcards match first. Wildcards must match a whole DNS label. e.g. ``*.foo.com`` and *.bar.foo.com are valid, however ``*bar.foo.com`` or ``*-bar.foo.com`` is invalid Domains are also used for SNI matching if the loadbalancer type is HTTPS Domains also indicate the list of names for which DNS resolution will be done by VER

<a id="nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--containers--liveness_check"></a>
### Nested Schema for `workload_choice.stateful_service.containers.liveness_check`

Read-Only:

- `health_check_choice` (Attributes) HealthCheckChoice Specifies action taken to determine health of a container (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--containers--liveness_check--health_check_choice))
- `healthy_threshold` (Number) HealthyThreshold Number of consecutive successful responses after having failed before declaring healthy. In other words, this is the number of healthy health checks required before marking healthy. Note that during startup and liveliness, only a single successful health check is required to mark a container healthy.
- `initial_delay` (Number) InitialDelay Number of seconds after the container has started before health checks are initiated
- `interval` (Number) Interval Time interval in seconds between two health check requests.
- `timeout` (Number) Timeout Timeout in seconds to wait for successful response. In other words, it is the time to wait for a health check response. If the timeout is reached the health check attempt will be considered a failure.
- `unhealthy_threshold` (Number) UnhealthyThreshold Number of consecutive failed responses before declaring unhealthy. In other words, this is the number of unhealthy health checks required before a container is marked unhealthy.

<a id="nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--containers--liveness_check--health_check_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `workload_choice.stateful_service.containers.liveness_check.health_check_choice`

Read-Only:

- `exec_health_check` (Attributes) ExecHealthCheck Specifies the run in container action to use for health check requests Exit status of 0 is treated as live/healthy and non-zero is unhealthy (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--containers--liveness_check--health_check_choice--exec_health_check))
- `http_health_check` (Attributes) HttpHealthCheck Specifies details for HTTP GET health check requests (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--containers--liveness_check--health_check_choice--http_health_check))
- `tcp_health_check` (Attributes) TCPHealthCheck Specifies port to use for TCP connection for health checks (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--containers--liveness_check--health_check_choice--tcp_health_check))

<a id="nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--containers--liveness_check--health_check_choice--exec_health_check"></a>
### Nested Schema for `workload_choice.stateful_service.containers.liveness_check.health_check_choice.exec_health_check`

Read-Only:

- `command` (List of String) Command Command is the command line to execute inside the container, the working directory for the command  is root ('/') in the container's filesystem. The command is simply exec'd, it is not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions ('|', etc) won't work. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell.

- `path` (String) Path Path to access on the HTTP server.
- `port` (Attributes) Port Name or number of the port to access on the container. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workload_choice--stateful_service--containers--liveness_check--health_check_choice--http_health_check--port))
